title: 2006 AMC 12B Problem 23
statement: Isosceles \(\triangle ABC\) has a right angle at \(C.\) Point \(P\) is inside \(\triangle ABC,\) such that \(PA = 11,\) \(PB = 7,\) and \(PC = 6.\) Legs \(\overline{AC}\) and \(\overline{BC}\) have length \(s = \sqrt{a + b\sqrt{2}},\) where \(a\) and \(b\) are positive integers. What is \(a + b?\)

solutions.text:
Rotate \(\triangle ABC\) by \(90^\circ\) about \(C,\) sending \(A\) to \(B\) and \(P\) to \(P'.\) Then \(CP' = CP = 6\) and \(\angle PCP' = 90^\circ,\) so \(\triangle PCP'\) is an isosceles right triangle with \(PP' = 6\sqrt2.\)

Also \(BP' = AP = 11.\) Since \((6\sqrt2)^2 + 7^2 = 72 + 49\) \(= 121 = 11^2,\) triangle \(BPP'\) has a right angle at \(P.\) Hence \(\angle BPC = \angle BPP'\) \(+ \angle P'PC = 90^\circ\) \(+ 45^\circ = 135^\circ.\)

By the Law of Cosines in \(\triangle BPC,\) \[ \begin{aligned} &BC^2 = 6^2 + 7^2 \\ &\quad {}- 2 \cdot 6 \cdot 7 \cos 135^\circ \\ &\quad = 85 + 42\sqrt2. \end{aligned} \]

So \(s^2 = 85 + 42\sqrt2,\) giving \(a = 85,\) \(b = 42,\) and \(a + b = 127.\)

Thus, the correct answer is E.
hints: Rotate \(\triangle ABC\) by \(90^\circ\) about \(C\) so that \(A\) maps onto \(B\)
The image of \(P\) forms an isosceles right triangle with \(P,\) which pins down \(\angle BPC\)
